transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Time: 10:00am PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Partnerships), Aaron (Solstice Head of Integrations), Priya (Solstice Platform Eng), Diego (Product), Nora (Security)

Summary:
Quick sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Solstice's managed ML infra, and joint solution options (co-sell listing + joint ref-arch doc). Confirmed technical owners and next steps to get a staging listing up for the marketplace pilot.

Topics: Marketplace listing manifest, reference architecture diagram, integration points (SSO, KMS, VPC peering), Terraform/Helm artifacts, security review, timeline for joint solution announcement.

Action items (also captured above): see metadata list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call — we wanted to focus on marketplace listing + the reference arch for Solstice's managed ML offering. Samir will lead on the tech pieces.
[00:25] Aaron (Solstice): Yeah thanks, we have a handful of folks so we can cover infra and security. Our goal is to get a marketplace listing that points customers to a one-click deploy + redwood connector, and a joint ref-arch showing network and key management.
[00:45] Samir (Redwood): Great, from previous chats we saw Solstice wants a listing that supports both hosted and dedicated Redwood flows — that means we need to list supported deployment modes, required IAM roles, and an example terraform/helm. The marketplace manifest typically needs: icons, screenshots, short/long descriptions, listing tags, and the deployment template.
[01:10] Priya (Solstice): On the terraform side we already have a module for provisioning VPC peering and role bindings, but we need guidance on the exact IAM permissions Redwood expects for the connector and for any service account that calls Redwood's private endpoints.
[01:35] Samir (Redwood): We'll share our recommended least-privilege policy. For dedicated flows, note that customers may want reserved capacity — the listing should mention how the handoff to Redwood Dedicated is initiated (e.g. via account config or partner ent). Also call out SSO options — SAML/OIDC — for provisioning and console access.
[02:00] Nora (Solstice): From security, we need to be explicit about data at rest encryption, KMS integration, logs, and audit capabilities. Does Redwood expose audit logs per tenant?
[02:20] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we can provide per-tenant audit logs and support KMS/HSM integrations, and we have SOC 2 and ISO attestations. We'll attach the security pack. Expect some redaction on the initial public listing but the private partner listing can include more detail.
[02:45] Diego (Solstice): For the joint solution brief — curious how you typically structure the architecture diagram. Do you want a high-level box diagram or a sequence flow?
[03:00] Samir (Redwood): Both. High level for marketplace customers (how Solstice instances connect to Redwood endpoints, network flows) + an appendix with sequence flow for Provision -> Token exchange -> Inference. We'll include examples for prefix caching, batching config, and recommended quantization profiles for cost savings.
[03:30] Aaron (Solstice): Good. On listing metadata: billing model, region availability, and support SLAs should be clear. We might add a line about latency expectations for hosted vs dedicated.
[03:50] Samir (Redwood): We'll provide typical p95 numbers for the models we ship and note that dedicated capacity has SLA-backed latency guarantees. Also include estimated token costs and a link to Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[04:10] Priya (Solstice): Operationally, we need a sample terraform that creates the connector, injects keys via Secrets Manager, and configures route tables. We can reuse our module if you provide the required variables.
[04:35] Samir (Redwood): We'll draft a minimal terraform snippet. Important notes: 1) avoid embedding long-term API keys — use short-lived creds with a token exchange; 2) outline IP allowlist ranges for inbound callbacks if any; 3) show how KV cache and prefix caching are optional.
[05:05] Nora (Solstice): Also need to validate that logs and telemetry don't leak customer data. Do you have guidance for redaction?
[05:25] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we'll share our telemetry policy — there are options to disable or filter PII. For private deployments we can do customer-managed logging.
[05:45] Aaron (Solstice): Vendor questionnaire — I think our procurement will run it; can Redwood pre-populate answers for marketplace partners?
[06:00] Maya (Redwood): We can pre-fill the security questionnaire and attach our SOC2 report. We'll send the docs as part of the checklist.
[06:15] Diego (Solstice): Timing — Solstice is aiming for a soft launch of the marketplace listing in early May. Is that feasible?
[06:30] Samir (Redwood): Yes, if we lock down artifacts this month. Key path: marketplace manifest + terraform + security Q answered + staging verification. That matches a ~6–8 week window.
[06:50] Priya (Solstice): One technical question: for VPC connectivity, do you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink? We have customers in both patterns.
[07:05] Samir (Redwood): We support both; PrivateLink is preferred for cross-account-managed endpoints in some clouds, peering is simpler in others. We'll document both patterns in the ref-arch and include a decision table.
[07:30] Aaron (Solstice): Any blockers on co-marketing or joint announcement? We want to align legal approvals and a short one-pager.
[07:45] Lena (Redwood): From partnerships we'll draft a co-sell brief and recommended messaging. Legal typically needs the final listing and a short MSLA excerpt. We can coordinate.
[08:00] Priya (Solstice): For testing, will Redwood run an initial smoke test against our staging account?
[08:15] Samir (Redwood): Yes, we'll run a connectivity and inference smoke test and a perf run for a 1k token chat to get latency/cost estimates. Plan to capture p50/p95 and token consumption in the spreadsheet.
[08:40] Nora (Solstice): Regarding encryption, if we use customer-managed KMS keys, are there limitations on key rotation?
[08:55] Maya (Redwood): Customer-managed KMS is supported; key rotation is supported but we need to coordinate re-encryption windows if using cached artifacts. We'll document recommended rotation cadence.
[09:15] Diego (Solstice): Do you have a recommended quantization profile for medium latency but lower cost? Our customers care about inference quality too.
[09:30] Samir (Redwood): We'll include our Optimize suggestions: int8 for embeddings and conversational models where quality tolerates it, bf16 for higher fidelity; plus per-model tradeoffs. We'll attach benchmark numbers.
[09:50] Aaron (Solstice): Ok let's talk manifest specifics — does Redwood need a special consumer-facing UI flow for the connector?
[10:05] Maya (Redwood): Marketplace UI needs a deploy button linking to a partner-hosted template. We can accept a cloud marketplace template or a private listing with a redirect. We will add a 'Get started' flow that passes customer metadata to Solstice for provisioning.
[10:30] Priya (Solstice): We'll prepare an AMI/helm chart and the terraform. We'll also set up a service account for Redwood to use for the smoke tests.
[10:45] Samir (Redwood): Please don't hand over long-lived keys; we'll request a short-lived token or an IAM role assumption. We'll document the token exchange flow in the ref-arch.
[11:10] Nora (Solstice): For the security pack, which artifacts should we expect? Attack surface docs, encryption details, SOC2 cert, a sample DPA?
[11:25] Maya (Redwood): Correct — SOC2, ISO letter, DPA template, audit log spec, and our redaction/PII policy. We'll attach all in the checklist.
[11:45] Diego (Solstice): Anything else around joint pricing or trial? We want to offer a limited trial credit for customers that install via the marketplace.
[12:00] Lena (Redwood): We can discuss trial credit; typically handled via a joint offer that requires a tag in the marketplace manifest. We'll loop in GTM.
[12:20] Aaron (Solstice): Ok wrap up — let's confirm owners and due dates.
[12:30] Maya (Redwood): Recap: Redwood to share marketplace checklist, sample manifest, security pack (due 2026-03-17). Samir to produce initial ref-arch and terraform snippet (due 2026-03-19). Solstice to provision staging and invite Redwood (due 2026-03-20). Solstice to return security questionnaire (due 2026-03-18). Next sync: schedule ref-arch review week of 2026-03-23.
[12:50] Priya (Solstice): Sounds good, I'll set up the staging and send invites.
[13:05] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[13:20] Aaron (Solstice): Thanks, bye.

References mentioned: Redwood marketplace checklist (link to be shared), sample terraform snippet (to be attached), SOC2 & security pack (to be shared), performance spreadsheet (to be used for p50/p95 numbers).
